comparison: Perfect agreement on the rationale for automated methods (C32-C35). Both accept the sample size calculations and time-efficiency arguments. OpenEval notes the Cochran formula details aren't fully provided, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the rationale by praising the automated pipeline.

Strong agreement on human RE study findings (C81-C89, C91). Both recognize fiber-type specificity and myofibrillogenesis as the primary mechanism. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=7) and modest p-value as limitations, while peer reviewers emphasize the value of human data confirming mouse findings without raising statistical concerns.

Strong agreement on FIM-ID method development (C4-C6, C92-C94). Both praise the innovation and accessibility. OpenEval notes the 'high resolution and contrast' claim is somewhat subjective, while peer reviewers uniformly endorse the method without qualification.

Agreement on sample preparation optimization (C46-C48, C52). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the optimization process, while peer reviewers focus on praising the methodology and resulting image quality without detailed critique.

Agreement on validation rigor (C53-C54). OpenEval notes strong statistical correlation but limited sample (8 ROIs, single fiber), while peer reviewers emphasize 'extensive validation' and 'solid validation' without noting sample size limitations.

Strong agreement on EM comparison validation (C59-C66). Both recognize comprehensive validation across fiber types. OpenEval notes modest sample size and EM measurement limitations, while peer reviewers uniformly praise the validation without raising these concerns.

Agreement on fiber type classification methodology (C55-C56). OpenEval describes the autofluorescence approach as 'creative and well-justified,' while peer reviewers accept the fiber type distinctions without objection in their analyses.

Strong agreement on MOV study findings (C67-C80). Both recognize myofibrillogenesis as primary mechanism. OpenEval notes the 'most robust' claim is interpretive and that both mechanisms contribute, while peer reviewers endorse this as a 'fundamental discovery' without qualification.

Partial agreement on cross-species consistency and novelty (C7, C95-C103). Both recognize the value of two-species validation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to single timepoint limitations and inability to determine temporal relationships, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, endorsing it as a major discovery.

Agreement on historical context and knowledge gap (C26-C27). OpenEval supports the characterization but cautions the 'no study has shown' claim should be verified carefully. Peer reviewers accept the historical perspective, with Reviewer 2 praising it as a strength.

Agreement that mechanisms remain uncertain (C110-C111). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for acknowledging unknown mechanisms and future research needs. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting single timepoint precludes mechanism assessment, treating this as an accepted limitation.

OpenEval evaluates background claims and knowledge gap identification (C1-C3, C8-C16) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers implicitly accepted the background by recognizing study novelty.

OpenEval evaluates EM limitations characterization (C28-C31) as SUPPORTED but notes severity is somewhat overstated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers praised FIM-ID as an alternative to EM.
